newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. plans $340 mln school funding boost.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. plans $340 mln school funding boost.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson said Tuesday his revised 1997-1998 budget plan would boost education funding by $340 million.

The budget revision, scheduled for release on Wednesday, will include an additional $230 million to reduce class sizes, $60 million to fund standardized testing, and $50 million to provide Internet techology to students, Wilson said in a statement.
Earlier this week, Wilson unveiled a $440 million welfare-to-work plan that included $50 million to capitalize the state infrastructure and economic development bank.
The Republican governor also proposed a $225 million package to aid the state's cash-strapped cities and counties as part his revised 1997-1998 budget plan.
State officials said Wilson's proposals reflect California's recent economic gains.
According to a report issued last week by the state's legislative analyst, revenues from the state's three major taxes were up $520 million in April.
The April gain brought cumulative 1996-1997 revenues to $825 million above Wilson's January budget estimate, the legislative analyst said.
At this rate, revenues over the current year and the next fiscal year combined will exceed the governor's January budget estimate by $2 billion, the report said.
